Run : end_manifest() also wrote timestamped CSV. Reading back shows structured record live alongside project:
code: # example_cleaning.R # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # A self-contained example of the manifest workflow. Run it with: # #   script <- system.file("examples", "example_cleaning.R", package = "manifest") #   source(script) # # Because it is run via source(), begin_manifest() auto-detects this file's # path and end_manifest() can back-fill the CRITERIA / CODE columns from the # `#:` comments below. The timestamped CSV is written under tempdir(). # # Comment key: #   #:   Manifest criteria  - appears in the CRITERIA column of the manifest #   ##   Dev / internal note - ignored by manifest #   #    Ordinary comment    - ignored by manifest # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------  library(dplyr) library(manifest)  ## -- Simulate a raw dataset --------------------------------------------------- set.seed(42) d <- data.frame(   id    = 1:1000,   x     = rnorm(1000, mean = 8, sd = 3),   state = sample(c("MN", "SD", "ND", "WI", "IA"), 1000, replace = TRUE),   year  = sample(2018:2023, 1000, replace = TRUE),   score = rnorm(1000, 50, 15) )  ## -- Open the manifest -------------------------------------------------------- begin_manifest(   data         = d,   description  = "Simulated dataset created to demonstrate package functionality",   build_script = "compile_data.R",   output_dir   = file.path(tempdir(), "manifest"),   dataset_name = "package_demo_data",   verbose      = TRUE )  ## QA note: x values were validated against source registry on 2024-01-15 #: {name} Drop outliers in X #: Omit records where X statistic exceeds 10 (outliers per pre-reg criteria) d <- mfilter(d, x <= 10)  ## We originally considered all 5 states; ND/WI/IA dropped for sample size #: {name} Study geography #: Restrict study to Minnesota and South Dakota (primary catchment states) d <- mfilter(d, state %in% c("MN", "SD"))  #: {name} Study time period #: Limit to study period 2020-2022 d <- mfilter(d, year >= 2020, year <= 2022)  ## Score < 0 is a data entry artifact; confirmed with PI on 2024-02-03 #: Remove records with invalid scores (score < 0 indicates data entry error) d <- mfilter(d, score >= 0)  ## -- Close the manifest, write the CSV, print the summary --------------------- end_manifest(d) library(manifest)  script <- system.file("examples", "example_cleaning.R", package = "manifest") source(script) #> Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.4.3 #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union #> [manifest] Started. Initial N = 1,000 #>  #> ------ Data Manifest ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #>                    STEP DROPPED DROPPED_PCT REMAIN REMAIN_PCT #>                   START      NA               1000       100% #>  (1) Drop outliers in X     248       24.8%    752      75.2% #>     (2) Study geography     471       47.1%    281      28.1% #>   (3) Study time period     134       13.4%    147      14.7% #>                     (4)       0        0.0%    147      14.7% #>                                                                     CRITERIA #>  description{Simulated dataset created to demonstrate package functionality} #>    Omit records where X statistic exceeds 10 (outliers per pre-reg criteria) #>      Restrict study to Minnesota and South Dakota (primary catchment states) #>                                              Limit to study period 2020-2022 #>    Remove records with invalid scores (score < 0 indicates data entry error) #>                                         CODE #>                       source{compile_data.R} #>                     d <- mfilter(d, x <= 10) #>    d <- mfilter(d, state %in% c("MN", "SD")) #>  d <- mfilter(d, year >= 2020, year <= 2022) #>                  d <- mfilter(d, score >= 0) #>  #> ---  Saved --- C:\Users\jdlec\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpMvKWlk/manifest/package_demo_data_manifest_20260811_135858.csv #> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ out_dir  <- file.path(tempdir(), "manifest") csv_file <- tail(sort(list.files(out_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)), 1)  knitr::kable(read.csv(csv_file, check.names = FALSE))

title: Getting started with manifest
text: begin_manifest(data, ...) opens log records starting row count. Two arguments worth calling : description — sentence dataset, stored START row. build_script — path script assembled raw data (often distinct cleaning script annotating). recorded manifest points back data’s origin. mfilter(data, ...) drop-replacement dplyr::filter(). applies filter records row delta. Pair #: comment line supply rationale automatically. end_manifest(data) parses script #: comments, back-fills CRITERIA / CODE columns, prints summary table, writes CSV. manifest_log() lets peek running log point end_manifest().

code: library(dplyr)  set.seed(1) roster <- data.frame(   id     = 1:20,   region = sample(c("A", "B"), 20, replace = TRUE),   active = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 20, replace = TRUE) )  begin_manifest(   roster,   description  = "Toy roster to demonstrate log_step()",   output_dir   = file.path(tempdir(), "roster-manifest"),   dataset_name = "roster",   verbose      = FALSE )  # A normal filter, tracked automatically: roster <- mfilter(roster, active)  # A de-duplication that filter() can't express — log it by hand: roster <- roster[!duplicated(roster$region), ] roster <- log_step(roster, criteria = "Keep one representative record per region")  manifest_log() #>   STEP DROPPED DROPPED_PCT REMAIN REMAIN_PCT #>  START      NA                 20       100% #>    (1)       8       40.0%     12      60.0% #>    (2)      10       50.0%      2      10.0% #>                                           CRITERIA CODE #>  description{Toy roster to demonstrate log_step()}      #>                                                         #>          Keep one representative record per region
